text:
maya: Drafting a really short, customer-facing mini-warmup playbook to attach to onboarding emails. Aim: <3 API calls, low QPS, reversible, and clear telemetry for CS. Quick feedback? :clipboard:

dinesh.cs: Thumbs up. Customers like 1-page things. Include an explicit reassurance: no model updates, no extra retention beyond normal logs.

alex.sre: Operationally, keep it: 1) small prefill (3 canonical prompts) 2) one streaming probe 3) 30m quick recheck. Use a short TTL (30-60m) and an ephemeral flag so keys auto-expire.

maya: Customer snippet (Python requests) to vary from our usual curl examples so it feels fresh for docs:

```
import requests
url = "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate"
headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer <KEY>", "X-Prefill-TTL": "45m"}
for p in ["Short summary: A","Short summary: B","Short summary: C"]:
    r = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json={"model":"redwood-lite-1","input":p})
    print(r.status_code)
# then open a streaming connection (SSE/WS) to confirm chunking
```

rachel.ops: Nice. Add a one-line FAQ for customers: "This warmup does not change your model or retention settings 14 it only reduces the likelihood of a slow first response."

alex.sre: Telemetry names: emit `warmup.run_ok` and `warmup.run_err`. Push an account attribute `warmup.last_status` and `warmup.attempts`. CS dashboard should show last_run, status, and a tiny histogram of first-token latency pre/post.

dinesh.cs: For renewal signal: if `warmup.last_status=error` and `warmup.attempts>=2` within 48h, create a CRM task: tag `needs-warm-handhold`.

maya: Edge-case ops notes: keep probe `max_tokens` low (<=20) and `batch_size` to 1 or 2 for these runs so we don't influence autoscaler. If you see 429s, back off with exponential jitter and try a single probe after 60s.

alex.sre: Include rollback snippet for SRE/ops (internal):
```
# internal-only: clear ephemeral prefill for account
curl -X POST https://internal.redwood.local/admin/cache/clear \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <ADMIN>" \
  -d '{"account_id":"ACCT999","scope":"warmup"}'
```

rachel.ops: Also note ownership: CS owns the customer-facing copy, eng-platform owns dashboard card and telemetry, eng-runtime owns runaway error alerts.

cs-bot: Action: create dashboard card for account view displaying warmup status (owners: cs-team, eng-platform). Reminder added. :bell:

maya: I'll produce two artifacts: 1) a one-page customer quick-start (short, with Python & curl examples, FAQ line), and 2) an internal triage checklist for CS+SRE that maps telemetry to actions. I'll post drafts in #customer-success tomorrow morning for a fast pass. :rocket:
